item.text:
The archive supports **two modest proposals** for a free community educational display. The venue is only possible, not booked, and its dates need confirmation with staff ([venue.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/venue.txt)). Mara has one weekend and a $30 maximum ([request.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/request.txt)).

1. **A movable “changing shoreline” paper demonstration.** Use white card, blue paper, scissors, and masking tape to show how moving bands can represent a changing shoreline. The prototype used card, blue offcuts, and scissors; the workshop notes say the movable bands made changes easy to notice ([materials.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt), [demo-notes.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/demo-notes.txt)). Pattern FW-7 is described as one folded card with three horizontal slits, but there is no finished stencil ([shape-diagram.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt)). Mara and her collaborator permit its use in a free community display, with credit to both makers; commercial resale is excluded ([folded-water.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/folded-water.txt)).  
   **Next steps:** Check that the shelf materials are still available ([craft-box.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt)); make and test a paper model; credit both makers; and confirm the display date. The older two-slit draft conflicts with the later three-slit workshop record, and the archive has no final-authoritative signoff ([old-copy.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt)). The abandoned motorized lightbox is not a practical option because it was never ordered and is unavailable ([old-plan.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/old-plan.txt)).

2. **A small Tide Lines text-and-observation display.** Pair Mara’s short captions with the three dated water-level observations and invite visitors to consider how a crossing changes with the tide ([text-fragments.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt), [observations.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt)). Mara permits reuse of her written notes and captions in free public educational displays ([tide-notes.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)). The observations are field notes, not a scientific dataset, so describe them that way.  
   **Next steps:** Draft a concise, text-only handout or table display. If printing is available, up to twelve black-and-white pages cost $8, though printer availability should be checked on the day ([printing.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/printing.txt)); the separate copy-shop quote is $8 for up to twelve pages and expires next month ([printing-quote.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/printing-quote.txt)). Confirm the date and budget before printing.

I would leave the photo and sound assets out of either proposal. The photo agreement requires separate written consent for public display, and none is recorded; the recording’s public-use permission is unconfirmed ([photo-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt), [sound-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/sound-terms.txt)). The historical claim about the inlet path moving inland in 1981 also needs checking against its original reference before publication ([research.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt)).

The archive does not establish that supplies remain available, that the printer will work, or that the library table is booked. Both concepts look feasible within the stated time and budget if those practical details check out; no rights clearance beyond the specific written permissions above is established.
